Design and implement the recovery side of a second-generation digital steering model. Historical speed caps fixed corner-entry over-command but made high-speed countersteer physically unreachable. We need normal keyboard/touch cornering to be speed-shaped while preserving emergency opposite-lock authority.

Audit available vehicle state (yaw rate, body sideslip/drift angle, steering state, speed) and choose the minimum safe state needed to distinguish ordinary corner steering from genuine oversteer/countersteer recovery. Do not add forces, fake grip, hidden stability control, or change analog mouse/wheel rack behavior. Prefer a narrowly scoped recovery escape path that can temporarily allow substantially more opposite lock and faster slew only when the car is actually rotating/sliding enough to need it. Avoid triggering full-lock just because the driver changes direction in a normal chicane.

Read AGENTS.md and PHYSICS_CONVENTIONS.md. Add deterministic mirrored tests for induced oversteer recovery, normal left-right direction changes, release, and high-speed recovery authority. Run conventions, digital steering, M5 transient/oversteer diagnostics, strict validation, and build. If stateful recovery is unsafe in the current architecture, propose the smallest robust alternative and prove it with tests.
